**Verdict**
Mostly positive, with important caveats. Kishida’s 2024 record shows repeated institutional steps to wall off political finance and succession from personal/factional capture. The strongest negative evidence is the funding scandal and factional survival politics, but I found no direct proof that family or business interests drove contracts, licensing, law enforcement, or foreign policy decisions.

**Positive**
- [Prime Minister’s New Year press conference](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/04kaiken2.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 4, 2024 | Kishida said the LDP would cooperate with prosecutors, invited external experts, and framed reform as transparent rule-making. That supports separation from private factional interests by leaning on outside scrutiny rather than insider control. | QIDs: `7B.3`, `7B.2`, `6B.9`, `6B.7`
- [Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 30, 2024 | Kishida apologized over the funding scandal, launched the Political Reform Headquarters, and promised transparency and legal reforms. That is direct evidence of trying to separate party finance from state power. | QIDs: `7B.3`, `7B.2`, `6B.9`, `6B.7`
- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 21, 2024 | He said the Political Funds Control Act was amended, disclosure thresholds were lowered, and a third-party body for inspections and audits should be created. This is the clearest 2024 evidence of building a constraint on private-money influence over politics. | QIDs: `7B.3`, `6B.9`, `6B.7`
- [Prime Minister’s statement on the LDP presidential election](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/14kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | August 14, 2024 | Kishida said the race should be transparent, with free and vigorous debate, and that he would step aside and support the successor chosen by vote. This supports a reading that he did not try to convert office into personal entrenchment. | QIDs: `7B.3`, `6B.9`, `7B.1`
- [Statement on the Nuclear Regulation Authority finding at Shika](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/14kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 14, 2024 | Kishida said the Nuclear Regulation Authority found no safety issues and that any restart would still require rigorous screening under post-Fukushima standards. That is evidence of formal, expert-led regulation rather than private or political favoritism. | QIDs: `7B.3`, `6B.9`, `6B.6`
- [Statement by Prime Minister Kishida on Ukraine peace](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202406/15ukraine.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 15, 2024 | Kishida framed Japan’s support around the UN Charter and international law and rejected force or coercion. That is evidence foreign policy was publicly justified in legal terms, not personal or family interest. | QIDs: `7B.3`, `6B.6`, `6B.1`
- [Japan-NATO summit press conference](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/11kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 11, 2024 | Kishida reported concrete Japan-NATO outcomes like information sharing, cyber/space cooperation, and support for Ukraine. This reads as ordinary alliance policy with public justification, not evidence of private-interest capture. | QIDs: `7B.3`, `6B.1`, `6B.6`

**Mixed / Negative**
- [Embattled Japan PM faces ethics committee to save popularity and budget](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362) | Reuters | February 28, 2024 | Reuters reported the funding scandal forced Kishida into defensive political management around popularity and the budget. That is negative context: public decision-making was under pressure from political survival, even if
I’m narrowing to finance reform, factional capture, and any trace of private-interest influence on state decisions; if I don’t find direct evidence, I’ll say so explicitly.
